newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sees $8 bln labor liabilities over 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sees $8 bln labor liabilities over 5 yrs.

text.p: Venezuela will have to pay some $8 billion over five years to cover labor liabilities related to the country's social security reforms, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said on Tuesday.

The cost is equivalent to two percent of gross domestic Product each year. Still, the country -- buttressed by windfall oil revenues and better tax collection -- would be "solvent through time and can finance this structural, social and political change," Matos told Congress.
Venezuela's crucial Labor Law reform, expected to be passed by Congress later Tuesday, forms part of a wider overhaul of the social security system, including pension fund recapitalization.

"We're going to comply with this promise," Matos said, adding that as a result the country's stock of debt had risen to $40 billion from $29 billion at the end of 1996. That includes the government's recognition of its outstanding $3 billion debt with the central bank, he said.
